dedupe_keys.name: senmes spanish national space weather service sector status and data

description: SeNMEs, the Spanish National Space Weather Service, is run by the Space Weather Group of the University of Alcalá and was developed in national research programme projects. Its portal is organised by the Sun, the interplanetary medium, the radiation environment and the Earth, and it shows a colour-coded status (grey no data, green calm, yellow minor activity or pre-alert, orange moderate, red intense, magenta severe) for sectors affected by space weather: aviation, communications, GNSS, oil and gas pipelines, geological prospecting, satellites, the electricity sector, insurance and rail transport, each with the time of its last update (for example 26 September 2026 at 14:07 UTC). Some functions need a login or registration, and an English version is offered. The university reserves intellectual property rights but allows use of the content for educational or scientific purposes with a clear citation of the source; access to the status pages is free. Caveats: the status is a summary indicator, and the methods behind each sector level are not described on the home page. Coverage is Spain, with global solar context. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response analysis of space weather effects on power grids, pipelines, rail signalling, GNSS and aviation; related records are the LAMP space weather data and SCiESMEX.
